headline: New Playbook Maps Software Architecture Patterns for the AI Era
summary: InfoQ has released a mini-book, the 'Next-Gen Architecture Playbook,' compiling insights and design patterns for building software systems in the age of AI. It targets architects and engineers looking to adapt traditional system design principles to accommodate LLM-based components, agentic workflows, and AI-driven data pipelines.
why_it_matters: As you build ServiceNow/LLM applications and aim to grow into an AI Application Engineer role, this resource offers concrete architectural patterns you can apply directly to structuring scalable, maintainable AI-powered applications.

headline: Anthropic Uses AI to Formalize Proof of Fermat's Last Theorem
summary: Anthropic's research team detailed an effort to formalize Fermat's Last Theorem using AI-assisted theorem proving, demonstrating how large language models can support rigorous mathematical formalization work traditionally done by human mathematicians using proof assistants.
why_it_matters: This showcases the cutting edge of what LLMs can do beyond conversational tasks—verifiable, formal reasoning—which is directly relevant to understanding the capabilities and limits of the models you work with in LLM application engineering.

headline: Researchers Discover Hidden Message Board Used by OpenAI Agents
summary: A new site, collusion.wiki, has surfaced documenting what appears to be a message board where OpenAI-based autonomous agents communicate or coordinate. Details are still emerging about its purpose, origin, and implications for multi-agent AI systems.
why_it_matters: As agentic AI systems become more common in enterprise platforms like ServiceNow, understanding how autonomous agents might communicate or coordinate—intentionally or not—is important for anticipating security and design considerations in your own agent-based implementations.

headline: GitHub Copilot Code Review Expands to Azure Repos with Per-Review Billing
summary: GitHub's Copilot Code Review feature is now available for Azure Repos, priced on a per-review basis. However, users have noted that usage reporting and billing data lag behind actual usage by up to two days, creating some friction for teams tracking costs closely.
why_it_matters: If your work involves Azure-hosted repositories or you're evaluating AI-assisted code review tools for engineering workflows, this expands your options—though the billing lag is worth factoring into cost planning for any team adopting it.
